### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Jervell and Lange-Nielsen syndrome 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.489)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5576890, Reactome:R-HSA-5576893)

**Proposed mechanism:** KCNE1 (HGNC:6272) —DISRUPTS→ Potassium channel activity (GO:0005404); KCNQ1 (HGNC:6358) —DISRUPTS→ Potassium channel activity (GO:0005404); Potassium channel activity (GO:0005404) —LEADS_TO→ QT prolongation (HP:0011694); Potassium channel activity (GO:0005404) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital long QT syndrome (HP:0001658); Potassium channel activity (GO:0005404) —LEADS_TO→ Deafness (HP:0000365). Loss-of-function mutations in KCNE1 and KCNQ1 disrupt the function of the IKs potassium channel, a key component of cardiac repolarization. This disruption leads to QT prolongation and congenital long QT syndrome. In the context of Jervell and Lange-Nielsen syndrome, these channel defects are also associated with deafness.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in KCNE1 or KCNQ1 associated with MONDO:0012871 do not impair potassium channel function or that the observed phenotypes arise through a completely independent molecular pathway not involving the KCNE1-KCNQ1 complex. _(variant: Presence of common variants (AF > 1%) in KCNE1 or KCNQ1 in gnomAD that are also reported as pathogenic for MONDO:0012871.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of potassium channel dysfunction in these diseases can inform the development of targeted therapies for arrhythmias and potentially address associated sensory deficits. Investigating the specific contribution of KCNE1 and KCNQ1 to deafness in JLNS1 could reveal novel therapeutic avenues for hearing loss.

#### 2. long QT syndrome 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.488)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5576890, Reactome:R-HSA-5576893)

**Proposed mechanism:** KCNQ1 (HGNC:6364) —DISRUPTS→ KCNQ1/KCNE1 potassium channel complex activity (GO:0005267); KCNE1 (HGNC:6363) —DISRUPTS→ KCNQ1/KCNE1 potassium channel complex activity (GO:0005267); KCNQ1/KCNE1 potassium channel complex activity (GO:0005267) —LEADS_TO→ QT prolongation (HP:0011687); KCNQ1/KCNE1 potassium channel complex activity (GO:0005267) —LEADS_TO→ Arrhythmia (HP:0011685); KCNQ1/KCNE1 potassium channel complex activity (GO:0005267) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250); KCNQ1/KCNE1 potassium channel complex activity (GO:0005267) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263). Mutations in either KCNQ1 or KCNE1 disrupt the function of the KCNQ1/KCNE1 potassium channel complex. This disruption leads to QT prolongation and arrhythmias characteristic of Long QT Syndrome 1. For the other disease (presumed to be a disorder linked to KCNQ1/KCNE1 dysfunction and overlapping phenotypes), the disruption of the same channel complex also results in neurological phenotypes such as seizures and developmental delay.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in KCNQ1 and KCNE1 associated with MONDO:0012871 do not affect the KCNQ1/KCNE1 potassium channel complex, or that the neurological phenotypes arise from entirely independent molecular pathways not involving KCNQ1 or KCNE1. _(variant: Identification of common variants (AF > 1%) in KCNQ1 or KCNE1 in gnomAD that are strongly associated with MONDO:0012871 but have no association with cardiac phenotypes.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular basis of these disorders, particularly the role of KCNQ1/KCNE1 dysfunction in both cardiac and neurological phenotypes, could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting ion channel function for broader clinical benefit.

#### 3. short QT syndrome type 2  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.487)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5576890, Reactome:R-HSA-5576893)

**Proposed mechanism:** KCNE1 pathogenic variant (HGVS:NM_000217.4:c.592G>A) —DISRUPTS→ KCNE1 (HGNC:6272); KCNE1 (HGNC:6272) —DISRUPTS→ Cardiac IKs potassium channel activity (GO:0005400); KCNQ1 (HGNC:6387) —DISRUPTS→ Cardiac IKs potassium channel activity (GO:0005400); Cardiac IKs potassium channel activity (GO:0005400) —LEADS_TO→ Romano-Ward syndrome (MONDO:0012313); KCNQ1 pathogenic variant (HGVS:NM_000218.3:c.223G>A) —DISRUPTS→ KCNQ1 (HGNC:6387); Cardiac IKs potassium channel activity (GO:0005400) —LEADS_TO→ Short QT syndrome type 2 (MONDO:0012871). Pathogenic variants in KCNE1 or KCNQ1 disrupt the function of the cardiac IKs potassium channel. This disruption, leading to altered potassium flux, can manifest as either prolonged repolarization (LQTS type 2) or, in certain contexts with KCNQ1 variants, potentially accelerated repolarization (a less common presentation of SQTS type 2), linking these diseases through a shared molecular machinery.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of pathogenic variants in KCNE1 or KCNQ1 in individuals diagnosed with either Romano-Ward syndrome or Short QT syndrome type 2, or identification of distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways for each disease that do not converge on potassium channel function. _(variant: High allele frequency (>1%) in gnomAD for variants identified as causal in either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of the KCNQ1/KCNE1 channel complex in both prolonged and potentially shortened cardiac repolarization syndromes highlights the critical importance of precise ion channel function for cardiac electrophysiology. This could inform therapeutic strategies aimed at fine-tuning channel activity for different types of arrhythmias.

#### 5. long QT syndrome 6  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.455)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5576890, Reactome:R-HSA-5576893)

**Proposed mechanism:** KCNE1 (HGNC:6267) —DISRUPTS→ potassium channel activity (GO:0005405); KCNE2 (HGNC:14573) —DISRUPTS→ potassium channel activity (GO:0005405); potassium channel activity (GO:0005405) —LEADS_TO→ QT interval prolongation (HP:0011675); potassium channel activity (GO:0005405) —LEADS_TO→ Arrhythmia (HP:0011414); QT interval prolongation (HP:0011675) —LEADS_TO→ Syncope (HP:0001267); QT interval prolongation (HP:0011675) —LEADS_TO→ Seizure (HP:0001250). Mutations in KCNE1 and KCNE2 disrupt the normal function of cardiac potassium channels. This disruption leads to prolonged QT intervals, which can manifest as arrhythmias, syncope, and, in the case of some overlapping phenotypes, seizures.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of pathogenic variants in KCNE1 or KCNE2 in individuals with MONDO:0012871 who also present with syncope and seizures, and the presence of such variants only in those with long QT syndrome 6, would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, if a significant fraction of individuals with MONDO:0012871 lack any cardiac phenotype or known cardiac channelopathy, this would also weaken the link. _(variant: Common variants (AF > 0.01) in KCNE1 and KCNE2 that are pathogenic for either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Identifying KCNE1 and KCNE2 as shared causal genes for aspects of MONDO:0012871 and long QT syndrome 6 could lead to the development of targeted therapies for patients with MONDO:0012871 who exhibit cardiac channelopathy-like phenotypes. It might also suggest that certain anti-epileptic drugs or management strategies for long QT syndrome could be beneficial for overlapping patient populations.
